accepted.question_text: For every sufficiently large odd integer n and every 2-regular graph F on n vertices, can the complete graph K_n be decomposed into edge-disjoint copies of F so that every edge of K_n lies in exactly one copy?

evidence.quote: We show that for all large n, the complete graph on n vertices can be decomposed into edge-disjoint copies of any given 2-regular graph of order n.

accepted.question_text: For all sufficiently large orders n, can the complete graph be decomposed into a prescribed collection of 2-factors, where each 2-factor is a spanning 2-regular graph?

evidence.quote: We also resolve the Hamilton-Waterloo problem for large n, which asks for a decomposition of the complete graph into prescribed 2-factors.

accepted.question_text: For every sufficiently large even integer n and every 2-regular graph F on n vertices, can the graph obtained from K_n by deleting a perfect matching be decomposed into n / 2 - 1 edge-disjoint copies of F?

evidence.quote: here we ask for a decomposition of Kn minus a perfect matching into n/2 − 1 copies of any given 2-regular graph F on n vertices. Theorem 1.3 covers this case.

accepted.question_text: For every fixed maximum degree bound Delta, does there exist n_0 such that whenever n > n_0 and F_1, ..., F_t are graphs on the same n vertices, each F_i is r_i-regular with r_i at most Delta, and the total degree sum r_1 + ... + r_t equals n - 1, the complete graph K_n can be decomposed into edge-disjoint copies of F_1, ..., F_t?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.4. For all ∆ ∈ N, there is an n0 ∈ N such that the following holds for all n > n0. Let F1, . . . , Ft be n-vertex ri-regular graphs with ri ≤ ∆ and i∈[t] ri = n − 1. Then there is a decomposition of Kn into F1, . . . , Ft.

accepted.question_text: If G is an n-vertex r-regular graph with even degree r at least (3/4)n plus a lower-order o(n) term, and F is any 2-regular graph on n vertices, must G decompose into edge-disjoint copies of F?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.5. Suppose G is an n-vertex r-regular graph with even r ≥ 3/4 n + o(n) and F is a 2-regular graph on n vertices. Then G decomposes into copies of F.

accepted.question_text: If G is an n-vertex even-regular graph with degree at least (2/3)n plus a lower-order o(n) term, and F is a 2-regular graph on n vertices whose cycles all have even length, must G decompose into edge-disjoint copies of F?

evidence.quote: It might also be true that 3/4 can be replaced by 2/3 in Conjecture 1.5 if F consists only of even cycles.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Clearly, one can generalise Conjecture 1.5 in this direction, e.g. to determine the decomposition threshold for Kr-factors.

evidence.quote: Clearly, one can generalise Conjecture 1.5 in this direction, e.g. to determine the decomposition threshold for Kr-factors.
